# Independent contract review — frozen NADIN sources

The current 14 public branch heads and trees are pinned in frozen-inputs.json.
The behavioural baseline is original tag v7.6, not a previous test implementation.
Only a reproduced failure can trigger a runtime edit. Candidate repairs must pass
their failure cases, valid countercases, the applicable complete matrix and a new
search round on the resulting frozen candidate.

Contracts fixed before the new experiments:

1. Manual audio/PDF renaming preserves both files when the final normalised name
   already belongs to another file; a legitimate distinct rename still works.
2. Deletion moves each source into recoverable storage. Two different tunes with
   the same basename cannot erase each other's retained bytes, even in one second.
3. Where the existing upload implementation retains previous versions, repeated
   successful replacements cannot erase a retained version and keep the latest
   current payload. Selection cancellation or rejected input changes no current file.
4. A multi-file upload cannot silently merge distinct inputs into one normalised
   destination. A rejected batch preserves the installation's prior bytes.
5. Simultaneous accepted media mutations cannot overwrite another source, a
   retained version or a duration rename. Busy handling is bounded and recovers.
6. Read/export workflows preserve source bytes, permissions, current/archive
   separation, literal headings/order/repetitions and forScore identities.
7. Original Main's normal editing, configuration and installation-owned data keep
   their established semantics. New protections must accept the valid counterpart
   of every rejected destructive action.
8. Later stages retain their own authentication, layouts, optional federation and
   conversion behaviour. A repair must not import an unrelated later-stage design.

This pass begins with new concrete media/editor experiments rather than first
rerunning the existing passing suites. Earlier test totals are historical evidence.
All experiments use local disposable copies and synthetic bytes. No production
installation, user account, music file or external recipient is touched.
